userStories.title: Thread handoff types and action rules
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Mirror C2's thread handoff wire types and derive the ordered action availability in pure web logic.

**Motivation** — The web also cannot see any of C2's state: `apps/web/lib/thread-types.ts` lacks `writtenPaths`, `publishedSha`, `specPublished`, `lastWrite`, `handoff` and `session.stale`.

**Approach** — `apps/web/lib/thread-types.ts` — Baseline: `ThreadSession` without `stale`, `ThreadDto` without the C2 fields, `ThreadDetailDto` with only `sendRefusal`. Target: `ThreadSession` gains `stale?: true`; new exported `ThreadWriteResult`, `ThreadHandoffJob { jobId: string; state: string; stateReason: string | null }`, `ThreadHandoff { plan: ThreadHandoffJob | null; run: ThreadHandoffJob | null }`; `ThreadDto` gains `writtenPaths: string[]`, `publishedSha: string | null`, `specPublished: boolean`, `lastWrite: ThreadWriteResult | null`; `ThreadDetailDto` gains `handoff: ThreadHandoff` (US-001).

Read-only wire mirror: `ThreadSession { jobId; state: 'live' | 'closed' | 'failed'; resumed; contextReset; reason: string | null; at; stale?: true }`; `ThreadWriteResult = { kind: 'published'; jobId; at; sha; paths: string[]; ignored: string[] } | { kind: 'publish_failed'; jobId; at; reason } | { kind: 'discarded'; jobId; at; sha } | { kind: 'discard_failed'; jobId; at; reason }`; `ChatThreadHandoff { plan: ThreadHandoffJob | null; run: ThreadHandoffJob | null }` with `ThreadHandoffJob { jobId; state; stateReason: string | null }` (the latest PLAN / RUN of the thread by `queuedAt`). Mirror jobId/at/sha/reason as strings, as in the API domain.

### Action rules (US-001, US-003)

`lib/thread-handoff.ts` (pure, no Vue):

```ts
export type HandoffAction = 'publish' | 'plan' | 'run' | 'discard'
export type HandoffBlock =
  | 'nothingToPublish' | 'turnRunning' | 'handoffBusy' | 'notPublished'
  | 'sessionActive' | 'notPlanned' | 'planNotCompleted'
export interface HandoffActionState { enabled: boolean; reason: HandoffBlock | null }

export function isHandoffBusy(thread: ThreadDetailDto): boolean
export function handoffActionState(
  thread: ThreadDetailDto, messages: readonly ChatMessageDto[], action: HandoffAction,
): HandoffActionState
export function showActionBar(thread: ThreadDetailDto, isCreator: boolean): boolean   // US-003
export function showStaleBanner(thread: ThreadDetailDto): boolean                     // US-003
```

`isHandoffBusy` is true when `handoff.plan` or `handoff.run` is non-null and its `state` is not terminal (`isTerminalJobState`). `handoffActionState` is an ordered pipeline: the first check that fails gives the reason, and `enabled` is `reason === null`.

| Action | Checks, in order |
|---|---|
| `publish` | `writtenPaths` empty → `nothingToPublish`; `isHandoffBusy` → `handoffBusy`; `isTurnRunning(messages)` or `sessionLabel(thread)` is `starting` or `closing` → `turnRunning` |
| `plan` | `specPublished` false → `notPublished`; `isHandoffBusy` → `handoffBusy`; `activeJob` non-null → `sessionActive` |
| `run` | `handoff.plan` null → `notPlanned`; `isHandoffBusy` → `handoffBusy`; `handoff.plan.state` not `COMPLETED` → `planNotCompleted`; `activeJob` non-null → `sessionActive` |
| `discard` | `isHandoffBusy` → `handoffBusy`; `activeJob` non-null → `sessionActive` |

A live session (`activeJob` RUNNING, no turn running) does not block Publish: the API sends `THREAD_PUBLISH` to it. `showActionBar` = `isCreator && thread.archivedAt === null && thread.sendRefusal !== 'disabled'`. `showStaleBanner` = `thread.session?.stale === true`.

C3-D1: `ThreadDto.activeJob` is the thread's non-terminal THREAD job of any action (a session, or a PUBLISH / DISCARD action job); it carries no action field. The web treats "`activeJob` is non-null" as "a THREAD job is active" for Plan, Run and Discard (`sessionActive`), and reads a running turn the way `sessionLabel` and `isTurnRunning` already do for Publish.

**Scope** — In: required DTO fields, exported discriminated types, isHandoffBusy/handoffActionState and tests/lib/thread-handoff.spec.ts. Out: showActionBar/showStaleBanner implementations and components belong to US-003; controller/form to US-002; timeline to US-004; loaders/events to US-005. Any API or migration change is excluded.

**Interface** — The TypeScript declarations above bind the pure helper; the two visibility functions are added in US-003. Export ThreadWriteResult, ThreadHandoffJob and ThreadHandoff from lib/thread-types.ts and preserve all existing DTO fields.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit]: isHandoffBusy returns true for a thread whose handoff.run has state RUNNING.
AC-2 [unit]: isHandoffBusy returns false for a thread whose handoff.plan has state COMPLETED and whose handoff.run is null.
AC-3 [unit]: handoffActionState(thread, [], 'publish') returns { enabled: false, reason: 'nothingToPublish' } when writtenPaths is [].
AC-4 [unit]: handoffActionState(thread, [], 'publish') returns { enabled: false, reason: 'handoffBusy' } when writtenPaths is ['.nax/features/f/spec.md'] and handoff.plan.state is QUEUED.

AC-5 [unit]: handoffActionState(thread, messages, 'publish') returns { enabled: false, reason: 'turnRunning' } when the thread has one written path, an idle handoff and a message whose status is streaming.

AC-6 [unit]: handoffActionState(thread, [], 'publish') returns { enabled: false, reason: 'turnRunning' } when the thread has one written path, an idle handoff and activeJob: { id: 'j1', state: 'UPLOADING' }.
AC-7 [unit]: handoffActionState(thread, [], 'publish') returns { enabled: true, reason: null } when the thread has one written path, an idle handoff and activeJob: { id: 'j1', state: 'RUNNING' }.
AC-8 [unit]: handoffActionState(thread, [], 'plan') returns { enabled: false, reason: 'notPublished' } when specPublished is false and activeJob is non-null.
AC-9 [unit]: handoffActionState(thread, [], 'plan') returns { enabled: false, reason: 'sessionActive' } when specPublished is true, handoff is idle and activeJob is non-null.
AC-10 [unit]: handoffActionState(thread, [], 'plan') returns { enabled: true, reason: null } when specPublished is true, handoff is { plan: null, run: null } and activeJob is null.
AC-11 [unit]: handoffActionState(thread, [], 'run') returns { enabled: false, reason: 'notPlanned' } when handoff.plan is null.
AC-12 [unit]: handoffActionState(thread, [], 'run') returns { enabled: false, reason: 'handoffBusy' } when handoff.plan.state is QUEUED.
AC-13 [unit]: handoffActionState(thread, [], 'run') returns { enabled: false, reason: 'planNotCompleted' } when handoff.plan.state is FAILED and handoff.run is null.
AC-14 [unit]: handoffActionState(thread, [], 'run') returns { enabled: false, reason: 'sessionActive' } when handoff.plan.state is COMPLETED, handoff.run is null and activeJob is non-null.
AC-15 [unit]: handoffActionState(thread, [], 'discard') returns { enabled: false, reason: 'sessionActive' } when handoff is idle and activeJob is non-null.

routing.reasoning: Additive DTO mirror and pure ordered rules span a few files; session-sensitive action gating invokes the security override.

userStories.title: Controller actions and the Plan/Run form
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add controller handoff actions and a validated reusable Plan/Run form schema and request conversion.

**Motivation** — No page reaches them, so a creator cannot hand a brainstormed spec to nax from koda.

**Approach** — ### Controller actions and the dialog form (US-002)

`lib/thread-controller.ts` gains, using the existing private `postAction` and `reloadThread`:

- `publish()` → `POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/publish` with `{}`, then reload the thread.
- `discard()` → `POST .../discard` with `{}`, then reload the thread.
- `plan(body)` → `POST .../plan` with `body`, then reload the thread.
- `run(body)` → `POST .../run` with `body`, then reload the thread.
- `reloadThread()` becomes part of the returned `ThreadController` (the page calls it on a `fleet_job` event).

Each action resolves `{ ok: true }` on success and `{ ok: false, error }` with the thrown error on failure.

`lib/thread-handoff-form.ts`:

```ts
export function buildThreadHandoffSchema(t: Translate): z.ZodObject<...>   // { profiles, maxCostUsd, bashMode }
export type ThreadHandoffFormValues = z.infer<ReturnType<typeof buildThreadHandoffSchema>>
export const THREAD_HANDOFF_DEFAULTS: ThreadHandoffFormValues   // { profiles: [], maxCostUsd: 5, bashMode: 'raw' }
export interface ThreadHandoffBody { maxCostUsd: number; profiles?: string[]; bashMode?: BashMode }
export function toThreadHandoffBody(values: ThreadHandoffFormValues, command: 'PLAN' | 'RUN'): ThreadHandoffBody
```

- `profiles`: an array of at most `MAX_PROFILES` (`fleet.dispatch.validation.profilesMax`), each matching `PROFILE_NAME_RE` and not starting with `koda-job-` (`fleet.dispatch.validation.profileName`), no duplicates (`fleet.dispatch.validation.profileDuplicate`).
- `maxCostUsd`: `z.coerce.number()`, above 0, at most `MAX_COST_USD`, at most 4 decimals (`fleet.dispatch.validation.maxCost` for every failure).
- `bashMode`: `z.enum(['raw', 'gated', 'escalate'])`.
- `toThreadHandoffBody` always sends `maxCostUsd`; it sends `profiles` only when the list is non-empty, and `bashMode` only when `command` is `RUN`.

C3-D2: a 409 the bar did not predict (`threads.runnerOffline`, `threads.runnerOutdated`, `fleet.budgetPaused`, `threads.busy`, `fleet.dispatch` 422, a validation 400) is toasted with `extractApiError(error)`, as every other thread action is today. The web never parses an error message. The controller returns the opaque thrown instance; US-003 owns the toast.

C3-D4: money stays a string shown with `usd()` (web context A7). The Plan/Run dialogs send `maxCostUsd` as a number, as the dispatch form does. API routes already ship: Publish 200 `{ jobId: string | null }`, Discard 200 `{ jobId: string }`, Plan/Run 201 `DispatchResultDto`. The API defaults maxCostUsd to 5 and the ref to `feat/<feature>`.

Failure handling: Publish / Discard / Plan / Run answers 409, 422 or 400 → `{ ok: false, error }`; the page toasts `extractApiError(error)`; state reloads on the next event. Plan/Run dialog values invalid → the form shows the `fleet.dispatch.validation.*` message; nothing is emitted.

**Scope** — In: extend existing ThreadController/postAction actions and expose reloadThread, create form helper and behavioral controller/form tests. Out: dialog/component rendering and page action bindings belong to US-003; job-detail/event wiring belongs to US-005; timeline belongs to US-004. Moving a thread to another runner, and choosing the runner or the ref in the Plan/Run dialogs (the API pins the thread's runner and `feat/<feature>`) are excluded. `approvalTimeoutSec` in the Run dialog; a gated or escalate RUN uses the API's default ask timeout. No API or migration changes.

**Interface** — Extend the returned ThreadController with these signatures:
```ts
publish(): Promise<ThreadActionResult>
discard(): Promise<ThreadActionResult>
plan(body: ThreadHandoffBody): Promise<ThreadActionResult>
run(body: ThreadHandoffBody): Promise<ThreadActionResult>
reloadThread(): Promise<void>
```
The form's signatures above are binding; infer a concrete ZodObject implementation rather than treating the illustrative ellipsis as source code. Existing thread controller methods and behavior remain unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit]: createThreadController({ slug: 'web', threadId: 'th1', ... }).publish() calls the fake API's post with path /projects/web/threads/th1/publish and body {}.
AC-2 [unit]: after publish() resolves { ok: true }, the controller's thread ref holds the detail the fake API's get returned for /projects/web/threads/th1.
AC-3 [unit]: discard() calls the fake API's post with path /projects/web/threads/th1/discard and body {}.
AC-4 [unit]: plan({ maxCostUsd: 5 }) calls the fake API's post with path /projects/web/threads/th1/plan and body { maxCostUsd: 5 }.
AC-5 [unit]: run({ maxCostUsd: 2, bashMode: 'gated' }) calls the fake API's post with path /projects/web/threads/th1/run and body { maxCostUsd: 2, bashMode: 'gated' }.
AC-6 [unit]: plan({ maxCostUsd: 5 }) whose post rejects with an ApiError of code 409 resolves { ok: false, error } where error is that same ApiError instance.
AC-7 [unit]: reloadThread() on the returned controller calls the fake API's get with /projects/web/threads/th1 and sets thread to its result.
AC-8 [unit]: THREAD_HANDOFF_DEFAULTS equals { profiles: [], maxCostUsd: 5, bashMode: 'raw' }.
AC-9 [unit]: toThreadHandoffBody(THREAD_HANDOFF_DEFAULTS, 'PLAN') returns { maxCostUsd: 5 }.

AC-10 [unit]: toThreadHandoffBody({ profiles: ['native-ds', 'workflow'], maxCostUsd: 2.5, bashMode: 'gated' }, 'RUN') returns { maxCostUsd: 2.5, profiles: ['native-ds', 'workflow'], bashMode: 'gated' }.
AC-11 [unit]: toThreadHandoffBody({ profiles: ['native-ds'], maxCostUsd: 2.5, bashMode: 'gated' }, 'PLAN') returns { maxCostUsd: 2.5, profiles: ['native-ds'] }.
AC-12 [unit]: buildThreadHandoffSchema(t) parsing { profiles: [], maxCostUsd: 0.00001, bashMode: 'raw' } fails with an issue whose message is the translation of fleet.dispatch.validation.maxCost.

AC-13 [unit]: buildThreadHandoffSchema(t) parsing { profiles: ['koda-job-x'], maxCostUsd: 5, bashMode: 'raw' } fails with an issue whose message is the translation of fleet.dispatch.validation.profileName.

AC-14 [unit]: buildThreadHandoffSchema(t) parsing { profiles: ['a', 'a'], maxCostUsd: 5, bashMode: 'raw' } fails with an issue whose message is the translation of fleet.dispatch.validation.profileDuplicate.
AC-15 [unit]: buildThreadHandoffSchema(t) parsing THREAD_HANDOFF_DEFAULTS succeeds.

routing.reasoning: Standard controller and Zod form patterns with no new dependency; Publish/Discard mutate thread-session handoff state, invoking the security override.

userStories.title: Action bar, dialogs and the stale banner
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose creator-only Publish/Plan/Run controls and confirmed stale Discard on the thread page.

**Motivation** — No page reaches them, so a creator cannot hand a brainstormed spec to nax from koda.

**Approach** — ### Action bar, dialogs and the stale banner (US-003)

Components in `components/fleet/threads/`:

| Component | Props | Emits |
|---|---|---|
| `ThreadActionBar` | `thread: ThreadDetailDto`, `messages: ChatMessageDto[]`, `isCreator: boolean` | `publish`, `plan(body: ThreadHandoffBody)`, `run(body: ThreadHandoffBody)` |
| `ThreadPublishDialog` | `open: boolean`, `paths: string[]` | `update:open(value: boolean)`, `confirm` |
| `ThreadHandoffDialog` | `open: boolean`, `command: 'PLAN' | 'RUN'` | `update:open(value: boolean)`, `submit(body: ThreadHandoffBody)` |
| `ThreadStaleBanner` | `thread: ThreadDetailDto`, `messages: ChatMessageDto[]`, `isCreator: boolean` | `discard` |

- `ThreadActionBar` (`data-testid="thread-action-bar"`) renders nothing when `showActionBar(thread, isCreator)` is false. Otherwise it renders three buttons, `thread-action-publish`, `thread-action-plan` and `thread-action-run` (labels `fleet.threads.handoff.actions.{publish,plan,run}`). Each button is disabled when its `handoffActionState(...)` is not enabled, and the reason text `fleet.threads.handoff.blocked.<reason>` shows beside it (`data-testid="thread-action-<action>-reason"`).
- Publish opens `ThreadPublishDialog` (title `fleet.threads.handoff.publishDialog.title`): it lists `writtenPaths`, one `data-testid="thread-publish-path"` item each, and its confirm button (`thread-publish-confirm`) emits `confirm`; the bar then emits `publish` and closes the dialog.
- Plan and Run open `ThreadHandoffDialog` with `command` `PLAN` or `RUN` (titles `fleet.threads.handoff.planDialog.title` / `runDialog.title`). It is a vee-validate form over `buildThreadHandoffSchema(t)` with initial values `THREAD_HANDOFF_DEFAULTS`: profiles (`FleetTokenListInput`, `testId` `thread-handoff-profiles`), max cost (`thread-handoff-max-cost`) and, for `RUN` only, bash mode (`NativeSelect` with the prop `testid="thread-handoff-bash-mode"`, labels `fleet.bash.mode.*`). A valid submit (`thread-handoff-submit`) emits `submit(toThreadHandoffBody(values, command))`; the bar re-emits it as `plan` or `run` and closes the dialog.
- `ThreadStaleBanner` (`data-testid="thread-stale-banner"`) renders only when `showStaleBanner(thread)`: the title `fleet.threads.handoff.stale.title` and body `fleet.threads.handoff.stale.body` for every viewer. For the creator it adds a Discard button (`thread-stale-discard`, `fleet.threads.handoff.actions.discard`), disabled with `fleet.threads.handoff.blocked.<reason>` when `handoffActionState(thread, messages, 'discard')` is not enabled. It opens a confirm dialog (`fleet.threads.handoff.discardDialog.{title,body,confirm}`) whose confirm (`thread-discard-confirm`) emits `discard`.
- The page renders `ThreadStaleBanner` and `ThreadActionBar` between `ThreadControls` and `ThreadTimeline`, and binds `publish` / `plan` / `run` / `discard` to the matching controller methods through the existing `runAction` (a `{ ok: false, error }` result is toasted with `extractApiError(error)`).
- Test harness: component tests register `FleetTokenListInput` with `loadSfc` in `components`, and the real `NativeSelect` through `mountSfc`'s `fleetComponents: ['FleetNativeSelect']` (the `uiStubs` select is inert); the dialog primitives come from `uiStubs`, which render their content when `open` is true.

Action rules visibility: `showActionBar` = `isCreator && thread.archivedAt === null && thread.sendRefusal !== 'disabled'`. `showStaleBanner` = `thread.session?.stale === true`. Add these to the US-001 helper now, and consume the real handoffActionState rather than duplicating its ordered checks. The action bar is shown only to the thread creator, only when the thread is not archived and threads are enabled. Each button is disabled with a visible reason. Discard is offered only in the stale banner, not in the action bar. The API refuses Plan and Run with `threads.busy` while any job of the thread is active; the web disables both while a THREAD job is active (`sessionActive`).

C3-D2: a 409 the bar did not predict (`threads.runnerOffline`, `threads.runnerOutdated`, `fleet.budgetPaused`, `threads.busy`, `fleet.dispatch` 422, a validation 400) is toasted with `extractApiError(error)`, as every other thread action is today. The web never parses an error message.

C3-D3: the marker and card texts live under `fleet.threads.handoff.*` in `en.json` and `zh.json`. The existing `tests/i18n/fleet-locale-parity.spec.ts` checks the `fleet` tree's en/zh parity and bans `|` and `@` in every `fleet` message, so no new text may contain either (no vue-i18n plural forms). The disabled reasons and marker kinds render through dynamic keys, so `used-keys-exist.spec.ts` cannot see them; `tests/i18n/thread-handoff-keys.spec.ts` (US-003) and `tests/i18n/thread-handoff-marker-keys.spec.ts` (US-004) pin those key sets. US-003 adds actions, blocked, dialogs and stale keys; US-004 adds marker/card keys.

Failure handling: Plan/Run dialog values invalid → the form shows the `fleet.dispatch.validation.*` message; nothing is emitted. Publish / Discard / Plan / Run answers 409, 422 or 400 → `{ ok: false, error }`; the page toasts `extractApiError(error)`; state reloads on the next event.

**Scope** — In: four components, visibility helpers, page action bindings, bilingual locales, component/locale/page tests. Out: mixed timeline markers and job cards belong to US-004; job-loader/composable/project-stream wiring and existing page-global updates belong to US-005. The two existing page tests register no ThreadActionBar or ThreadStaleBanner, so those render as unresolved elements and read no C2 field; test new bindings in tests/pages/threads-detail-handoff-page.spec.ts, created here. Moving a thread to another runner, and choosing the runner or the ref in the Plan/Run dialogs are excluded. `approvalTimeoutSec` in the Run dialog is excluded.

**Interface** — Props/emits in the table above are binding. Visibility helper signatures:
```ts
export function showActionBar(thread: ThreadDetailDto, isCreator: boolean): boolean
export function showStaleBanner(thread: ThreadDetailDto): boolean
```
Use ThreadHandoffBody and the form defaults/schema/conversion created by US-002. Paths and every new runner-written value remain interpolation-only, never v-html. When US-005 adds useThreadHandoffJobs/useProjectEvents, this story's new page suite supplies both through globals and retains its US-003 assertions.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit]: ThreadActionBar mounted with isCreator: false over a thread with written paths renders no element with data-testid=thread-action-bar.
AC-2 [unit]: ThreadActionBar mounted with isCreator: true over a thread with writtenPaths: [] renders thread-action-publish-reason with the text of fleet.threads.handoff.blocked.nothingToPublish.
AC-3 [unit]: ThreadActionBar mounted with isCreator: true over a thread with specPublished: false renders thread-action-plan-reason with the text of fleet.threads.handoff.blocked.notPublished.
AC-4 [unit]: clicking an enabled thread-action-publish over a thread with writtenPaths: ['a.md', 'b.md'] renders two thread-publish-path items with the texts a.md and b.md.
AC-5 [unit]: clicking thread-publish-confirm in the open publish dialog makes ThreadActionBar emit publish exactly once.
AC-6 [unit]: opening the Plan dialog from an enabled thread-action-plan and clicking thread-handoff-submit with the default values makes ThreadActionBar emit plan with { maxCostUsd: 5 }.

AC-7 [unit]: opening the Run dialog from an enabled thread-action-run, selecting gated in thread-handoff-bash-mode and submitting makes ThreadActionBar emit run with { maxCostUsd: 5, bashMode: 'gated' }.
AC-8 [unit]: ThreadHandoffDialog mounted open with command: 'PLAN' renders no element with data-testid=thread-handoff-bash-mode.
AC-9 [unit]: ThreadStaleBanner mounted over a thread whose session.stale is true renders an element with data-testid=thread-stale-banner containing the text of fleet.threads.handoff.stale.title.
AC-10 [unit]: ThreadStaleBanner mounted with isCreator: true over a stale thread with a non-null activeJob renders the thread-stale-discard button with the disabled attribute set.

AC-11 [unit]: ThreadStaleBanner mounted with isCreator: true over a stale thread with activeJob: null and an idle handoff emits discard exactly once after thread-stale-discard then thread-discard-confirm are clicked.

AC-12 [unit]: in both en.json and zh.json, the keys under fleet.threads.handoff.blocked are exactly nothingToPublish, turnRunning, handoffBusy, notPublished, sessionActive, notPlanned and planNotCompleted, each with a non-empty text.
AC-13 [unit]: ThreadHandoffDialog mounted open with command: 'RUN', max cost set to 0 and thread-handoff-submit clicked emits no submit event.
AC-14 [unit]: on the thread page mounted with a stubbed useThread, the action bar's plan emit with { maxCostUsd: 5 } calls the stubbed controller's plan with { maxCostUsd: 5 }.

AC-15 [unit]: on the thread page mounted with a stubbed useThread whose publish resolves { ok: false, error: new ApiError(409, 'Runner offline') }, the action bar's publish emit makes the toast recorder receive the error Runner offline.

routing.reasoning: Four interactive components, real validated forms, page actions and bilingual dynamic-key seams span multiple modules; creator-only controls and session actions invoke the security override.

userStories.title: Timeline write marker and PLAN/RUN cards
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Render the latest Publish/Discard result and latest PLAN/RUN cards in a deterministic mixed thread timeline.

**Motivation** — The web also cannot see any of C2's state: `apps/web/lib/thread-types.ts` lacks `writtenPaths`, `publishedSha`, `specPublished`, `lastWrite`, `handoff` and `session.stale`.

**Approach** — ### Timeline markers and job cards (US-004)

`lib/thread-timeline.ts` (pure):

```ts
export interface HandoffJobs { plan: FleetJobDto | null; run: FleetJobDto | null }
export type ThreadTimelineEntry =
  | { kind: 'message'; key: string; message: ChatMessageDto }
  | { kind: 'write'; key: string; write: ThreadWriteResult }
  | { kind: 'job'; key: string; command: 'PLAN' | 'RUN'; handoff: ThreadHandoffJob; job: FleetJobDto | null }
export function buildThreadTimeline(
  messages: readonly ChatMessageDto[], thread: ThreadDetailDto, jobs: HandoffJobs,
): ThreadTimelineEntry[]
export interface WriteMarkerView { key: string; params: Record<string, string | number>; paths: string[]; ignored: string[] }
export function writeMarkerView(write: ThreadWriteResult): WriteMarkerView
```

- Keys: a message entry's `key` is the message `id`; a write entry's is `write:<jobId>`; a job entry's is `job:<jobId>`.
- A job entry's `job` is `jobs.plan` (or `jobs.run`) only when that detail's `id` equals the handoff's `jobId`; a detail for another job is ignored (`null`).
- Anchors: a write entry anchors at `write.at`; a job entry anchors at `job.queuedAt` when its `job` is non-null, and has no anchor otherwise.
- Order: messages keep their given order. Each anchored marker goes immediately before the first message whose `createdAt` is strictly later than the anchor (compared with `Date.parse`), or after every message when none is. Markers without an anchor go after every message. Markers at the same position are ordered by anchor ascending (no anchor last), then write before PLAN before RUN.
- `writeMarkerView`:

| `write.kind` | `key` | `params` | `paths` / `ignored` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `published` | `fleet.threads.handoff.marker.published` | `{ sha: sha.slice(0, 7), count: paths.length }` | `write.paths` / `write.ignored` |
| `publish_failed`, reason `branch_moved` | `fleet.threads.handoff.marker.publishFailedBranchMoved` | `{}` | `[]` / `[]` |
| `publish_failed`, other reason | `fleet.threads.handoff.marker.publishFailed` | `{ reason }` | `[]` / `[]` |
| `discarded` | `fleet.threads.handoff.marker.discarded` | `{ sha: sha.slice(0, 7) }` | `[]` / `[]` |
| `discard_failed` | `fleet.threads.handoff.marker.discardFailed` | `{ reason }` | `[]` / `[]` |

Components:

| Component | Props | Emits |
|---|---|---|
| `ThreadWriteMarker` | `write: ThreadWriteResult` | — |
| `ThreadJobCard` | `command: 'PLAN' | 'RUN'`, `handoff: ThreadHandoffJob`, `job: FleetJobDto | null`, `slug: string` | — |

- `ThreadWriteMarker` (`data-testid="thread-write-marker"`) renders `t(view.key, view.params)`, and, when `view.paths` is non-empty, a collapsible list of the paths (`thread-write-marker-path`) plus the ignored paths under `fleet.threads.handoff.markerIgnored`. Every value renders through `{{ }}` interpolation, never `v-html`.

userStories.title: Live job details, page wiring and the E2E journeys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Load and live-refresh handoff job details on the thread page and integrate the four scripted-runner browser journeys.

**Motivation** — PLAN and RUN job transitions publish no thread event, so even with the fields the page would not update while a job runs. #266 asks for a browser test of the #264 fix, which only has unit and integration coverage.

**Approach** — ### Live job details and page wiring (US-005)

`lib/thread-handoff-jobs.ts`:

```ts
export interface HandoffJobsDeps { api: { get: <T = unknown>(path: string) => Promise<T> }; slug: string }
export interface HandoffJobsController {
  jobs: Ref<HandoffJobs>
  sync: (handoff: ThreadHandoff) => Promise<void>
  refreshJob: (jobId: string) => Promise<void>
  isHandoffJob: (jobId: string) => boolean
}
export function createHandoffJobs(deps: HandoffJobsDeps): HandoffJobsController
```

- `sync(handoff)` records the handoff, then for each of `plan` and `run`: a null handoff entry sets that slot to `null`; an entry whose `jobId` and `state` equal the cached detail's `id` and `state` fetches nothing; any other entry fetches `GET /projects/:slug/fleet/jobs/:jobId` (path built with `apiPath`) and stores the result. On a failed fetch the slot keeps a cached detail with the same `id`, and is `null` otherwise; `sync` never rejects.
- `isHandoffJob(jobId)` is true when `jobId` equals the last synced `handoff.plan?.jobId` or `handoff.run?.jobId`.
- `refreshJob(jobId)` fetches the detail again and replaces its slot when `isHandoffJob(jobId)`; otherwise it does nothing. A failed fetch keeps the slot.
- `composables/useThreadHandoffJobs.ts`: `useThreadHandoffJobs(slug: string, thread: Ref<ThreadDetailDto | null>): HandoffJobsController` wires `createHandoffJobs` with `useApi().$api` and watches `thread.value?.handoff` (immediate), calling `sync` whenever it is non-null.
- The page calls `useThreadHandoffJobs(slug, controller.thread)` and `useProjectEvents(slug, { onFleetJob, onResync })`: `onFleetJob(event)` calls `controller.reloadThread()` and `handoffJobs.refreshJob(event.jobId)` when `handoffJobs.isHandoffJob(event.jobId)`, and does nothing otherwise; `onResync` calls `controller.reloadThread()`. The page passes `handoffJobs.jobs.value` and `slug` to `ThreadTimeline`.

### E2E journeys (US-005, C3-R4)

`tests/e2e/fleet-threads.e2e.spec.ts` gains four tests against the scripted v4 runner, each on its own thread and feature. They are verified with `bun run test:e2e -- fleet-threads` in `apps/web`; Playwright specs are not nax acceptance criteria.

1. **Crash mid-turn (#266):** after `text_delta` streams, the runner reports the THREAD job `FAILED` (`report(lease, [{ type: 'state', payload: { to: 'FAILED', reason: 'crashed' } }])`). Without a reload, the page's streaming indicator disappears, the message shows its errored marker, and `thread-stop` is gone.
2. **Idle close (#266):** after a completed turn, the runner uploads `session_closed { reason: 'idle' }` and reports `COMPLETED`. Without a reload, the session label leaves Live and `thread-end-session` is gone.
3. **Handoff:** the runner enrolls with `threadWrite: true`. During a session it uploads a `write_doc { path, bytes }` line for `.nax/features/<feature>/spec.md`; Publish becomes enabled and its dialog lists the path. Confirming delivers a `THREAD_PUBLISH` command; the runner uploads `published { sha, paths, ignored: [], specPresent: true }` and the write marker shows the short sha. After End session (the runner uploads `session_closed` and reports `COMPLETED`), Plan submits the dialog; the runner accepts the PLAN job's ASSIGN and reports `RUNNING` then `COMPLETED`, and the PLAN card shows Completed without a reload. Run submits; the runner uploads a tar bundle with a `workflow/result.json` whose outcome is `draft` (shape as in `bundle-ingest.workflow.spec.ts`) and reports `ESCALATED`; the RUN card shows the Draft outcome without a reload.
4. **Stale:** a session's `session_started` line carries `stale: true`; the banner shows, its Discard button is disabled with the `sessionActive` reason; after End session, Discard creates a DISCARD job; the runner uploads `discarded { tipSha }` and completes it, and the banner is gone.

Changed test seams:
- `apps/web/tests/pages/threads-detail-handoff-page.spec.ts` — created by US-003 for its page ACs; once the page calls `useThreadHandoffJobs` and `useProjectEvents`, its mounts supply both through `globals`, and it gains the US-005 page tests (the `onFleetJob` / `onResync` handlers and the RUN card from the loader's jobs); the US-003 assertions stay as they are.
- `apps/web/tests/helpers/mount-sfc.ts` — `NUXT_AUTO_IMPORTS` gains `'useThreadHandoffJobs'` so page tests can supply it through `globals` (US-005). Without it the harness never binds a test's useThreadHandoffJobs global and every thread page mount throws; no existing behaviour changes.
- `apps/web/tests/e2e/fixtures/scripted-runner.ts` — `ScriptedRunner.enroll` merges `threadWrite: true` into the thread capabilities when `opts.threadWrite` is set (US-005). Enrolments without it keep today's capabilities.
- `apps/web/tests/pages/threads-detail-page.spec.ts` — the page now calls `useProjectEvents` and `useThreadHandoffJobs`, which the harness injects as undefined; the mount's `globals` gain `useProjectEvents: () => undefined` and a `useThreadHandoffJobs` stub returning `{ jobs: ref({ plan: null, run: null }), sync, refreshJob, isHandoffJob: () => false }`, and the existing assertions stay as they are.
- `apps/web/tests/pages/threads-detail-actions-page.spec.ts` — the page now calls `useProjectEvents` and `useThreadHandoffJobs`, which the harness injects as undefined; the mount's `globals` gain `useProjectEvents: () => undefined` and the same `useThreadHandoffJobs` stub, and the existing assertions stay as they are.
- `apps/web/tests/e2e/fleet-threads.e2e.spec.ts` — gains the four journeys of "E2E journeys"; the existing create/send/Stop/read-only test stays as it is.

C3-R3 (RUN outcome): the RUN card reads workflow, resultPrUrl, costSpentUsd and escalationReason from GET /projects/:slug/fleet/jobs/:id. A failed detail fetch degrades the card to the state in handoff, with no error toast. Keep a same-id cached detail on a subsequent failed fetch as specified above; initial or changed-id failure renders null-detail fallback.

Failure handling: Job detail fetch fails → the card shows `handoff.state` and `stateReason` only; no toast. A cached job detail is for an older handoff job → ignored by the timeline (`job: null`). A `fleet_job` event for an unrelated job → ignored. Project event stream reconnects → `onResync` reloads the thread.

Seams: `useThreadHandoffJobs`'s watch is the only link from the thread to the loader; AC15 drives it with a real thread ref. HandoffJobs and ThreadTimeline jobs are consumed by the page; AC14 asserts the RUN card from loader jobs. reloadThread exposed in US-002 is consumed by onFleetJob; AC11/12 drive the handler. Use shared client-only useProjectEvents rather than opening another project EventSource.

**Scope** — In: injected loader, immediate-watch composable, page event subscription and timeline jobs/slug wiring, harness compatibility, optional runner write capability, four browser journeys and loader/composable/page tests. Out: component rendering and action forms are upstream US-003/US-004; do not change API, runner production code, migrations, workflow ingest or existing thread-stream crash fix. No thread-jobs endpoint, job threadId/filter, older-history storage, job-page backlink or online-dot updating. The four Playwright journeys are verified with bun run test:e2e -- fleet-threads, not as nax acceptance criteria.

**Interface** — The loader declarations above and this composable signature bind implementation:
```ts
export function useThreadHandoffJobs(
  slug: string, thread: Ref<ThreadDetailDto | null>,
): HandoffJobsController
```
Use HandoffJobs from US-004 and ThreadHandoff from US-001. Browser verification needs the e2e Postgres on port 5433, unique per-journey threads/features, valid workflow tar member and waitForHydration (never networkidle).

analysis:
Goal and done: deliver Fleet S5a-C3, the web-only final phase-C slice connecting thread-written specs to Publish, Plan, Run and stale Discard. The creator can hand off a spec through confirmed actions, all viewers can see the latest write result and latest PLAN/RUN, and RUN workflow outcomes and job transitions appear without manual reload. Preserve the five binding stories and sequential dependencies. All 75 explicitly numbered spec ACs are retained in their original stories; additional criteria enumerate failure-table behavior and regression guards explicitly requested by the refine audit. Optional hardening assertions remain in suggestedCriteria. Four browser journeys are implementation verification, not nax acceptance criteria. C1/C2 and workflow mode are upstream deployed dependencies; no API, migration, generated client, OpenAPI, fleet jobs-list or job-page modification is required.

Discovery and stack: codebase-memory MCP was not exposed; a capability request confirmed it unavailable, so discovery used direct reads and targeted searches. The supplied Next.js/Express detection is inaccurate: apps/web/package.json:6-15 uses Nuxt build/dev/typecheck, Jest and Playwright; dependencies at apps/web/package.json:24-45 include Nuxt 3, Vue, vee-validate and zod. The existing API controller uses Nest decorators (apps/api/src/fleet/threads/threads.controller.ts:79-96,136-151), not an Express implementation to extend. Follow .nax/mono/apps/web/context.md:1-79: hand-written Nuxt composables, API-owned domain rules, separate en/zh locales, and interpolation-only runner text apart from the already-sanitized assistant markdown exception. Rooted contextFiles/expectedFiles are repo-relative even though every story workdir is apps/web. Generated AGENTS.md files are not authoring sources. The redesign guidance at docs/ux/redesign/MASTER-PLAN.md:24-46 calls for existing semantic HSL tokens and preserving pinned shell/navigation; this feature adds local thread controls, not a redesign of shell, navigation or tokens. If implementation broadens to layout/navigation, follow that master plan's status/decision-log rule rather than creating a documentation story.

US-001 impact: apps/web/lib/thread-types.ts:43-80 currently has neither session.stale nor C2 writtenPaths/publishedSha/specPublished/lastWrite/handoff. Mirror the already-shipped shapes at apps/api/src/fleet/threads/domain/chat-thread.domain.ts:17-54: optional stale is true-only; write results are four discriminated variants, and handoff is latest plan/run by queuedAt. New lib/thread-handoff.ts is pure, with ordered refusal precedence, not a server authorization replacement. Reuse isTurnRunning (pending or streaming, apps/web/lib/thread-view.ts:66-69), sessionLabel (QUEUED/ASSIGNED starting, UPLOADING closing, RUNNING live, apps/web/lib/thread-view.ts:72-80), and isTerminalJobState (COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CRASHED/CANCELLED, apps/web/lib/fleet-jobs.ts:3-10). Treat every non-null activeJob as an active THREAD job; it has no action discriminator. Live idle RUNNING permits Publish; starting/closing or a running turn blocks it. Plan/Run/Discard require no activeJob according to their ordered pipelines. Unknown handoff states remain busy because they are not terminal. US-003 implements visibility helpers on the same new module.

Type dependents: targeted search shows thread-types imported by thread-controller.ts:13, thread-view.ts:6, thread-event-stream.ts:18, useThreads.ts:9, fleet-types.ts:7, thread list/header/timeline/message/composer/controls/question components, and tests/lib/thread-view.spec.ts:13, tests/lib/thread-controller.spec.ts:5, tests/lib/thread-controller-errors.spec.ts:4, tests/composables/useThread.spec.ts:4, useThread-lifecycle.spec.ts:5, useThreads.spec.ts:2, tests/pages/threads-page.spec.ts:8, tests/components/thread-list-table.spec.ts:6 and both existing detail-page suites. Required new fields can invalidate hand-built typed fixtures; use canonical empty C2 defaults where these fixtures need them, preserving existing assertions. The explicit runtime-sensitive fixture updates belong to US-004, not a broad refactor of unrelated behavior.

US-002 impact: the stateful injected controller at apps/web/lib/thread-controller.ts:26-68 already returns ThreadActionResult and holds Vue refs. reloadThread is private at :97-99; postAction at :258-268 catches POST or reload errors, posts {} by default, reloads after success, and resolves rather than rejects. Extend that exact pattern with four endpoints and expose reloadThread; do not alter send retry, optimistic echo, thread stream or poll lifecycle. Existing onThread already refreshes running-turn messages for the crash/close fix (#264) at :162-174. New form helper imports dispatch constants rather than introducing a second profile policy; apps/web/lib/fleet-dispatch.ts:10-16,34-42 provides the regex, reserved prefix, max count, max cost and four-decimal tolerance. Copy only relevant validations: full buildDispatchSchema requires repo/ref/feature/planFrom and has approval timeout rules not appropriate for this dialog. ThreadHandoffBody is a named interface; when passing it to postAction's Record<string, unknown>, use a compatible request object without weakening public types. Profiles stay string arrays, money input becomes a number, and PLAN omits bashMode. API contracts at apps/api/src/fleet/threads/dto/thread-handoff.dto.ts:5-25 allow optional profiles/maxCostUsd and RUN bashMode; the web intentionally always sends the default numeric cap 5. There is no runner/ref/approval-timeout field in these dialogs. Existing controller tests use fake deps and ApiError (apps/web/tests/lib/thread-controller.spec.ts:2-5,111,364-447).

US-003 impact: apps/web/pages/[project]/threads/[id].vue:22-29 already computes creator from auth user and thread.createdById, separately from canManage. Its runAction at :44-55 toasts extractApiError for any failed result. Insert banner and bar after ThreadControls and before ThreadTimeline (:62-76), and bind all four actions via runAction; no error-message parsing or speculative retry for runner/budget/busy failures. Creator visibility is not a new backend access-control system; API remains authoritative. Banner remains visible to non-creators without Discard. Add four components and locale subtree fleet.threads.handoff in both files. Dialogs use vee-validate/zod and existing token input/native select. NativeSelect's componentField-compatible v-model and lowercase testid prop are documented at apps/web/components/fleet/NativeSelect.vue:17-28; an inert select stub will not test bash-mode emission. Component harness at apps/web/tests/helpers/mount-sfc.ts:1-12 compiles real SFCs and resolves real lib helpers. Register FleetTokenListInput via loadSfc and FleetNativeSelect via fleetComponents, retaining open-aware dialog primitives. New tests/pages/threads-detail-handoff-page.spec.ts isolates new page bindings; existing detail-page suites do not register the new bar/banner and must preserve their assertions. Dynamic blocked key tests pin exactly seven keys. apps/web/tests/i18n/fleet-locale-parity.spec.ts:80-96 already checks fleet/nav parity; its remaining fleet-message checks disallow pipe and at-sign syntax. New text must avoid both characters, including plural messages.
